mainTopic: Which כהן stays טהור when a מת מצוה is found, and the source that a כהן גדול must bury a מת מצוה
overview: This amud finishes a list of pairs of כהנים who find a מת מצוה together. In each pair, the more important כהן stays טהור and the other one becomes טמא to bury the מת. An anointed כהן גדול ranks above a מרובה בגדים, a serving מרובה בגדים ranks above a משוח שעבר, and a כהן who stepped aside for קרי ranks above one removed for a מום. Then the גמרא asks a real question: does the משוח מלחמה or the סגן rank higher? A ברייתא says the משוח מלחמה becomes impure, but another ברייתא says he comes first. מר זוטרא explains the difference: for saving a life the משוח מלחמה comes first, and for טומאה the סגן comes first, because he must stay ready to replace the כהן גדול. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה. It notes that a כהן גדול or a נזיר who is alone must bury a מת מצוה. It then finds the source for the כהן גדול in the words 'for his father' in ויקרא 21:11.

steps.title: Anointed כהן גדול outranks a מרובה בגדים
steps.stepSummary: Between a כהן גדול anointed with שמן המשחה and a מרובה בגדים, the anointed one is preferred, because only he brings the פר for mistakes in all the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a High Priest of many garments: the one anointed with the anointing oil is preferable. The anointed one brings the bull that comes for all the מצוות, while the one of many garments does not bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going through a list of pairs of כהנים to decide which one should stay טהור. Here it compares a כהן גדול anointed with oil to one who became כהן גדול only by wearing the eight garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are real כהנים גדולים, but the anointed one has an extra law: if he rules wrongly, he brings a special פר as a קרבן חטאת. The מרובה בגדים does not bring this פר. That extra law shows the anointed one has the higher status, so he is the one who stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול anointed with the special anointing oil
A כהן גדול appointed by wearing the eight garments, without anointing
Preferable / ranks higher
The bull a משוח brings for a mistaken ruling about any prohibition (ויקרא 4:3)

steps.confusionAlert: In this list, 'עדיף' means this כהן is more important, so HE stays טהור, and the other one becomes טמא to bury the מת.

phrases.english: And one of many garments —
the one anointed with the anointing oil is preferable,
since the one anointed with the anointing oil —

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא פַּר הַבָּא עַל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת,
phrases.english: brings the bull that comes for all the מצוות,
while one of many garments does not bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ranking list that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An anointed כהן גדול outranks a מרובה בגדים because only he brings the פר for all the מצוות.

steps.title: מרובה בגדים outranks a משוח שעבר
steps.stepSummary: A serving מרובה בגדים is preferred over a משוח שעבר, because the first still does the עבודה and the second no longer does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A former anointed priest and one of many garments: the one of many garments is preferable, because he performs the service, while the former anointed priest is no longer fit for the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with the next pair. Now the less-honored מרובה בגדים actually wins, because he is the one serving right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anointing alone does not decide the ranking. A משוח שעבר was anointed but has stepped down, so he no longer does the עבודה in the מקדש. Doing the עבודה right now is the deciding factor here.

keyTerms.meaning: A formerly anointed כהן גדול who no longer serves (for example, one who filled in temporarily)
The service in the בית המקדש
Someone fit to do the עבודה

phrases.english: A former anointed priest and one of many garments —
the one of many garments is preferable,
since the one of many garments performs the service,
while the former anointed priest —
is not fit for the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרוּבֵּה בְגָדִים עָדִיף, דִּמְרוּבֵּה בְגָדִים עָבֵיד עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next pair in the same ranking list. It brings in a new deciding factor: actively serving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A serving מרובה בגדים outranks a משוח שעבר because he does the עבודה.

steps.title: One who stepped aside for an emission outranks one removed for a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who stepped aside because of קרי is preferred over one who stepped aside because of a מום, since the first can serve again tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who left because of his seminal emission and one who left because of his blemish: the one who left because of his emission is preferable, because he is fit for the service tomorrow, while the one who left because of his blemish is not fit for the service.
steps.whatsHappening: Another pair in the list. Both of these כהנים stepped down, so the גמרא looks at whether either one can come back to the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרי is a temporary problem: after immersion and nightfall, the כהן can serve again. A מום is permanent, so that כהן can never do the עבודה again. Being able to return to the עבודה gives the first כהן the higher rank.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission, which makes one temporarily טמא
A physical blemish that disqualifies a כהן from the עבודה
Fit / suitable

steps.whatToRemember: The easy cases follow one pattern: whoever is more connected to the עבודה (now, or soon) or has a special status ranks higher.

phrases.english: One who left because of his seminal emission
and one who left because of his blemish —
the one who left because of his emission is preferable,
since this one is fit for the service tomorrow,
while the one who left because of his blemish
is not fit for the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last easy pair in the list. It applies the 'fit for the עבודה' reason from step 2 to two כהנים who both stepped down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stepping aside for קרי (temporary) outranks removal for a מום (permanent).

steps.title: Dilemma: משוח מלחמה or סגן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ranks higher: the משוח מלחמה, who is fit for war, or the סגן, who is fit for the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a priest anointed for war and a deputy High Priest, which of them is preferable? Is the one anointed for war preferable, since he is fit for war? Or perhaps the deputy is preferable, since he is fit for the service?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא raises a real question with no obvious answer. It sets up two sides, and the answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משוח מלחמה has an anointing and a special job for war. The סגן is not anointed, but he can step in for the כהן גדול in the עבודה. The question is which counts more: anointing with a war role, or closeness to the עבודה (the reason that won in steps 2 and 3).

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a real open question)
The כהן anointed to speak to the army before battle (דברים 20:2)
The deputy of the כהן גדול
Or perhaps

steps.whyThisMatters: This question tests which earlier reason is stronger: having been anointed (step 1) or being fit for the עבודה (steps 2 and 3).

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
a priest anointed for war and a deputy High Priest,
phrases.notes: The משוח מלחמה is the כהן from דברים 20:2.

phrases.english: which of them is preferable?
Is the one anointed for war preferable, since he is fit for war,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא סְגָן עֲדִיף — דַּחֲזֵי לַעֲבוֹדָה?
phrases.english: or perhaps the deputy is preferable, since he is fit for the service?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה וּסְגָן, הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ עֲדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the easy cases, the גמרא moves to a hard case where the earlier reasons point in different directions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משוח מלחמה (anointed, fit for war) or the סגן (fit for the עבודה) should stay טהור.

steps.title: A ברייתא answers: the משוח מלחמה becomes impure, the סגן does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the משוח מלחמה and the סגן find a מת מצוה, the משוח מלחמה becomes impure and the סגן does not. This shows the סגן ranks higher here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא: The only difference between the משוח מלחמה and the סגן is this. If they were walking on the road and found a מת מצוה, the משוח מלחמה should become impure, and the סגן should not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question from the last step. When a מת מצוה is found, the משוח מלחמה is the one who becomes impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who must become impure is the one whose purity matters less. Since the משוח מלחמה is told to become impure, the סגן's purity is treated as more important. So in this case the סגן outranks him.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
A dead person with no one else to bury him; whoever finds him must bury him
He should become impure
The deputy כהן גדול

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
There is no difference between the one anointed for war and the deputy,
except that if they were walking along the road
and found a met מצוה,
the one anointed for war should become impure
and the deputy should not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ranks higher: the משוח מלחמה or the סגן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a case of a מת מצוה, the משוח מלחמה becomes impure and the סגן stays pure, so the סגן ranks higher

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the משוח מלחמה comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer with a ברייתא saying the משוח מלחמה comes before the סגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches: the משוח מלחמה comes before the סגן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite: the משוח מלחמה ranks higher than the סגן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא gave the סגן priority, and this one gives the משוח מלחמה priority. Both cannot be true in the same way, so the גמרא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? This opens a challenge from another ברייתא
Comes first, has priority

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The one anointed for war comes before the deputy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 5 with a ברייתא that seems to contradict it
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 5 that gives the סגן priority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives the משוח מלחמה priority, which contradicts the first

steps.title: מר זוטרא: saving a life versus staying pure
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא explains that the two ברייתות speak about different things. For saving his life, the משוח מלחמה comes first, because the people depend on him. For טומאה, the סגן comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: For saving his life, the משוח מלחמה is preferred. Why? Because many people depend on him. But for טומאה, the סגן is preferred.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא answers the contradiction. Each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of priority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Priority depends on the question being asked. If both are in danger, we save the משוח מלחמה first, because the army depends on him. If one must become impure, the סגן stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeping him alive, saving his life
Is preferred, ranks higher
Because many people depend on him

steps.confusionAlert: Neither one is simply higher than the other. Each one comes first in a different area: saving a life or staying pure.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
Regarding saving his life,
the one anointed for war is preferred.
What is the reason?
Because the many depend on him.
phrases.notes: In a time of war, the people rely on him.

phrases.english: And regarding impurity, the deputy is preferred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא speaks about a different kind of priority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other about who ranks higher
steps.terutzMaskana: The משוח מלחמה comes first for saving a life, and the סגן comes first for staying pure
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that rank is not one fixed ladder. Who comes first can change depending on what is at stake.

steps.title: Proof: the סגן exists to replace the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס supports the idea that the סגן must stay pure. The סגן was set up so he could serve in place of a disqualified כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: Why did they set up a סגן for the כהן גדול? So that if the כהן גדול becomes disqualified, the סגן can go in and serve in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up why the סגן comes first when it comes to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole job of the סגן is to be ready to replace the כהן גדול at any moment. If he became impure, he could not do that job. So his purity must be protected.

keyTerms.meaning: They set up, they established
A disqualification that stops him from serving
Serves in his place

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
Why did they set up a deputy for the High Priest?
So that if a disqualification happens to him,
the deputy can go in and serve in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of מר זוטרא's answer
steps.raayaObject: That the סגן comes first when it comes to טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס about why the סגן was set up
steps.whatToRemember: For saving a life, the משוח מלחמה comes first. For טומאה, the סגן comes first, because he must stay ready to replace the כהן גדול.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: each one alone must bury a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. The argument there is only about a כהן גדול and a נזיר walking together. If each is alone, he must become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue about a כהן גדול and a נזיר who are walking together. But if each one is alone, they are able to become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and points out what both sides agree on. A כהן גדול or a נזיר who is alone must bury a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument in the משנה is only about which of the two should become impure. That assumes each one, when alone, does become impure for a מת מצוה. This sets up the next question: where do we learn that?

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue as far as this
Together with each other
By himself, alone
Able (allowed and required) to become impure

phrases.english: They only disagree
phrases.notes: "They" are the תנאים in our משנה who argue about which of the two should become impure.

phrases.english: about a High Priest and a nazir
when they are walking together.
But each one by himself
is able to become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ranking discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that a כהן גדול or a נזיר who is alone must become impure for a מת מצוה

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a כהן גדול and a נזיר must become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule just stated. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול and a נזיר may not become impure even to bury their own close relatives. So the גמרא wants to know where we learn that a מת מצוה is different.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? A request for the source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a כהן גדול and a נזיר must become impure to bury a מת מצוה

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the verse is about a כהן גדול's relatives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what kind of dead people the verse 'על כל נפשות מת לא יבא' is talking about. It cannot be strangers, because a קל וחומר from a כהן הדיוט already teaches that. So the verse must be talking about relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Neither shall he go in to any dead bodies.' What is the verse talking about? If it means people who are not related to him, we would know that from a קל וחומר anyway. An ordinary כהן is allowed to become impure for his relatives, and still he may not become impure for strangers. So a כהן גדול, who may not become impure even for his relatives, surely may not become impure for strangers. So the verse must be talking about his relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from step 10 by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first works out which dead people the verse about the כהן גדול is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse is not needed to teach something that a קל וחומר already proves. A כהן גדול cannot become impure for strangers, because even a כהן הדיוט cannot. So the verse must be adding something new, namely that a כהן גדול may not become impure even for his relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: What case is the verse talking about?
Close relatives, the family members an ordinary כהן may become impure for
Distant people, meaning anyone who is not a close relative
A logical argument: if the lighter case has this rule, the stricter case surely has it too
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר is not where the ברייתא ends up. Its job is to show that the verse would be unnecessary if it were about strangers, so the verse must be about relatives.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"Neither shall he go in to any dead bodies"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:11, said about the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: What is the verse talking about?
If it is about distant people,
that can be learned from a קל וחומר:
Just as an ordinary כהן,
who does become impure for his close relatives,
still does not become impure for distant people,
then a כהן גדול, who does not become impure even for close relatives,
is it not logical that he does not become impure for distant people?
Rather, the verse is talking about close relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the source question of step 10 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא first shows that 'על כל נפשות מת לא יבא' is about relatives, which frees the next words of the verse to teach the rule about a מת מצוה.

steps.title: The word 'for his father' leaves room for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Relatives are already covered by the first part of the verse, so the words 'for his father' teach a limit. It is for his father that he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is for his father that he may not become impure. This shows that he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next words of the same verse, 'for his father', and draws a precise inference from them. This gives the source for the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the verse already forbids a כהן גדול to become impure for relatives, so 'for his father' would add nothing new as a plain ban. The גמרא therefore reads it as a limit: it is for his father that he may not become impure. From that limit it infers the opposite case: for a מת מצוה, he does become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: For his father, the next words in the verse
This shows that, used to draw the opposite conclusion from a phrase
A dead person with no one else to bury him, whom even a כהן גדול must bury

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול may not become impure for anyone, even his father. But the extra words 'for his father' show that he must become impure to bury a מת מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the source for the כהן גדול half of the question in step 10, and it supports the statement in step 9 that a כהן גדול walking alone must bury a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: And it is for his father that he does not become impure,
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק: 'for his father or for his mother he shall not defile himself.'

phrases.english: which shows that he does become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 11 (the first words of the verse already cover relatives) to read 'for his father' as a limit that leaves out a מת מצוה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן גדול must become impure to bury a מת מצוה, learned from the words 'for his father'.
